answer: Fingerprints are counted in echo, which means the distribution is public, and saffron lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a lagoon header, so 1149 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
